`curl`: make an HTTP request.

## Synopsis

<strong>curl</strong> \[<strong>-X</strong> <em>method</em>\] \[<strong>-H</strong> <em>header</em>\]... \[<strong>-d</strong> <em>data</em>\] \[<strong>-o</strong> <em>file</em>\] \[<strong>-iIfLs</strong>\] \[<strong>-A</strong> <em>agent</em>\] <em>url</em>

## Description

<strong>curl</strong> makes an HTTP or HTTPS request through the computer's internet card and writes what comes back to standard output. A URL without a scheme is <strong>http://</strong>'s.

The card reaches only the public internet: never the server's own machine or network (the server's settings may allow more, or less). It writes the headers HTTP needs itself (<strong>Host</strong>, <strong>Content-Length</strong>, <strong>Connection</strong>); a request can't set those.

## Options

<strong>-X</strong> <em>method</em>
: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH or OPTIONS.

<strong>-H</strong> <em>'Name: value'</em>
: A header; again for more.

<strong>-d</strong> <em>data</em>
: A body: the request is a POST, with <strong>Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded</strong> unless a header says otherwise. Again for more, joined with <strong>&</strong>.

<strong>-o</strong> <em>file</em>
: Writes to <em>file</em> instead.

<strong>-i</strong>
: Writes the response's status and headers first.

<strong>-I</strong>
: Makes a HEAD request: only its status and headers.

<strong>-L</strong>
: Follows redirects.

<strong>-f</strong>
: Fails on an HTTP error (400 or more): no output, exit 22.

<strong>-s</strong>
: Silent: no messages.

<strong>-A</strong> <em>agent</em>
: The User-Agent header.

## Exit status

0 when done; 2 for bad usage; 6 for an unknown host; 7 when it couldn't connect (refused, or the server forbids the address); 22 for an HTTP error with <strong>-f</strong>; 23 when the output can't be written; 28 when it timed out; 47 for too many redirects.

## Examples

```text
curl https://example.com/
curl -i -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"a":1}' https://example.com/api
curl -sL -o page.html example.com
```

## Notes

Real <strong>curl</strong> speaks many protocols and has hundreds of options; mcos's speaks HTTP and HTTPS, with these.
